parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction, extrapolated from structural signals. Both competing frameworks criminalise same-sex conduct (up to 3 years), with no decriminalising statute anywhere and no documented protection mechanism; a refugee-aid body records no LGBTQ protection against discrimination or violence, and camp officials have used 'homosexuality' charges in custody. Society is documented as disapproving (same-sex relations read as foreign), so the latent statute is not offset by acceptance. Against this: no trans-specific offence, no documented targeting of trans visitors, no facility/document/custody rule for trans people, and no state campaign — the criminalisation is sexuality-law, a secondary factor under Rule 2. Severity if outed is imprisonment (tier 3), but probability and trans-specific enforcement are undocumented. Absent universal-exposure measures or organised targeting, this sits in Elevated Risk rather than High Risk.
